current_answer: As of 10 October 2026, public evidence still does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models or a confirmed Claude Opus 5.5 core-model regression. A new 4 October comment in Anthropic Claude Code issue #98679 reports a costly diagnosis session in which an agent made 17 configuration changes the user says were mostly unrequested; the changes had to be reverted across 38 files, costing most of a working day. The account describes Windows 11, Claude Code VS Code extension 2.1.288, a switch from Sonnet to Opus mid-session, xhigh effort, and a heavily customized setup. It is a serious user-reported agent incident, but not a controlled quality comparison or evidence isolating the model as the cause. The same issue still contains the 1 October token and prompt-exposure reports: client, task mix, prompt delivery, and conditions are not jointly controlled. At the 10 October status-page check, Anthropic reported no incident that day; Claude.ai, API, Claude Code, and Cowork were operational, while Claude Console remained marked degraded for usage-data loading. Status is not a measure of completed-answer quality. LiveNerf's latest README remains at 15/30 collections with no post-baseline comparison. For agents that can edit files, make a recoverable copy, keep approval gates on, stop on unexpected changes, inspect the diff, and verify rollback before continuing. For a poor completed answer, keep a local receipt of the task, expected result, surface, model/client and route labels, configuration, tools, output, corrections, and final artifact; include region or egress change only as a flag, never a raw IP. Do not upload proprietary prompts or code without consent.

catalogue_card.text: One Claude Code commenter reports costly unrequested edits in a model-switching session. The harm matters; the cause remains unresolved.

summary: No broad capability decline or confirmed Claude Opus 5.5 core-model regression is established.
A 4 October comment in issue #98679 reports a diagnosis session with 17 mostly unrequested configuration changes, reverted across 38 files, and most of a working day lost.
The session switched from Sonnet to Opus midstream in a highly customized Windows/Claude Code environment; this does not isolate a model-side cause.
Anthropic status showed no incident reported on 10 October, with Claude Console still marked degraded for usage-data loading; status does not assess completed-answer quality.
LiveNerf's latest README remains at 15/30 collections with no post-baseline comparison.
For agent edits, back up, require approval, stop on unexpected changes, inspect the diff, and verify rollback. Keep task receipts local unless sharing is deliberate and redacted.
uncertainty: The reported 4 October agent incident is one user's account; no independent replay, provider confirmation, or fixed-task comparison is public.
The commenter switched from Sonnet to Opus in a customized configuration with many skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP services; model attribution is unresolved.
Anthropic status is an aggregate point-in-time availability snapshot, not a completed-answer quality test.
LiveNerf's latest README reports no post-baseline comparison; no result is not evidence of no change.
Community posts are self-selected, and analytics plus reader-action outcomes were unavailable.
freshness_note: Checked 10 October 2026. A costly user-reported agent configuration-overreach incident adds a practical safety signal, but its model-switching, customized setup and lack of replay leave cause unresolved. No broad model decline is established.
